threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still trust the bus timetable. Locals know it’s just a polite suggestion, not a promise.
Last night, a bloke serenaded us with a ukulele on the 50. Even the driver joined in, all the way to Brixton. Only in Streatham.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a group of kids using old traffic cones as soccer goals on the street, I knew Neukölln's spirit was unmistakably home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you hop on a tram, but if it’s a strike day, just grab a paddle board and take to the Spree for your commute instead.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they ignore the BART delays. Newcomers are still panicking at the announcement boards, while we just adjust our plans silently.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 19 Polk yesterday. Two folks arguing over a missing sandwich while a street performer belted out 'California Dreamin'. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists love to ask about La Rambla, but the real secret is the quiet plazas in Gràcia where you can hear the locals laugh, not just the street performers.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newcomer by their hesitance at the crossroads, staring at the street signs and fumbling with their Google Maps. They don’t know the shortcuts yet.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still stare at the Tube map like it’s a crossword puzzle. Locals know the shortcuts and which exits avoid the crowds.
Last week on the 313, a couple got off at the wrong stop, ended up at the old market. They lit a spliff right there and started dancing to music only they could hear.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I heard a busker playing Unholy's sax on the corner of Sonnenallee while someone tried to sell homemade pickles. Classic Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find a club where the DJ starts their set with the sound of a train door closing. That quirky vibe is pure Berlin.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: A true local knows that the taco trucks are better after 10 PM, especially when you're dodging the late-night BART delays.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 38Geary yesterday and the driver let a busker jump on for a quick tune. People were smiling, even in the Tenderloin rush. Classic SF moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think ‘Gràcia’ is just about Gaudí. They miss the quiet corners where locals sip vermut and chat about fútbol, oblivious to the crowds.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They always ask for a ‘bocata’ at cafes, not realizing it's just a sandwich. The locals know it’s called a ‘sandvitx’ here.
